subject: STAGING: eval-lane reserve request & procurement handshake
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: transient reserve for staging-eval lanes (6w)

Sean / David —

Quick ask from Product: Acme AI wants a short, dedicated staging lane to run an intensive eval sweep before their pilot launch. They need guaranteed GPU headroom for roughly 6 weeks (minimum). High level: 4x A100-equivalent GPUs (shared across 2 machines), reserved Monday–Friday 08:00–20:00 PT, best-effort outside those times.

Why: the eval runs are latency-sensitive and produce large KV-cache priming that makes cold starts expensive; if we rely on normal pooling they'll hit throttles and we risk a failed pilot.

What Product asks us to do:
- Approve a temporary carveout of 4 GPUs from the US West pool starting week of Nov 30 for 6 weeks
- Permit an autoscale policy override (allow burst to 6 GPUs for 2 short windows per week)
- Finance/Procurement are lining up a PO and 30-day payment terms; Marcus will handle deal ops.

Can Ops/Capacity confirm feasibility, constraints, and any compensating controls (preemption notice, fallbacks)? If we can't approve the autoscale override, please propose alternatives (e.g. scheduled reserved windows).

Thanks —
Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Product Manager, Dedicated Capacity
Redwood Inference

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 10:32:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: transient reserve for staging-eval lanes (6w)

Kim / Sean —

We can probably accommodate a transient carveout, but the autoscale override is the risky part. Current autoscale policy disallows forced bursts beyond reserved commitment without an approvals exception — primarily because it upsets capacity fairness and can cause tail latency to increase for other customers.

Questions / asks from Capacity ops:
- Please quantify peak qps / tokens/s expectations for the eval runs and duration of the "burst windows" (we need mean and 95th).
- Confirm whether the workloads are tolerant of preemption outside the Monday–Friday window (we can set an eviction notice + migrate KV-cache, but it's not instant).
- We'll need a signed justification doc and a capacity exception approval ticket (I created JIRA-RUN-879).

If Product can accept scheduled, short windows (e.g., Tue/Thu 09:00–13:00 and Wed 14:00–18:00) instead of open-ended burst, that reduces risk. Otherwise we can approve a controlled burst with strict guardrails:
- Burst opens only after a second confirmation from finance (PO received)
- Auto-fallback to lower-capacity model variant on sustained contention
- Ops retention of preemption rights with 30-min notice

I'll run a quick utilization simulation once we get the traffic numbers.

—David
David Kim
Head of Capacity & Allocations
Redwood Inference

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 23 Nov 2026 13:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: transient reserve for staging-eval lanes (6w)

Thanks David — attaching rough numbers from the eval team (see staging_eval_headroom.csv). TL;DR:
- Typical run: 120k tokens/min sustained for 45–90 minutes; peak bursts ~250k tokens/min for up to 20 minutes
- Expected weekly windows: two 4-hour blocks + one ad-hoc 1–2 hour sweep (we can pre-schedule the ad-hoc to avoid surprises)

Product is OK with scheduled windows as David suggested. Compromise proposal:
- Reserve 4 GPUs Mon–Fri 08:00–20:00 PT for 6 weeks (no use by other customers)
- Allow two scheduled burst windows per week (pre-booked slots, ops-approved), each up to +2 GPUs for up to 30 minutes. No open-ended autoscale.
- Product commits to provide run schedule 72 hours in advance for ad-hoc sweeps and to accept fallback to a slightly smaller model if preemption occurs.

Marcus: Acme legal/finance indicated they'll sign a pilot PO with net30 if we can confirm the reservation and runbook.

If that sounds acceptable, David/Laurai — can you confirm and we can route the PO?

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Solutions Lead, Strategic Pilots
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Kelly <ben.kelly@acme.ai>, Procurement - Acme AI <procurement@acme.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 24 Nov 2026 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: STAGING: eval-lane reserve request & procurement handshake

Ben —

Thanks for the quick response. Per Product & Ops, Redwood can provision a scheduled transient reserve as described (4 GPUs, Mon–Fri daytime, plus two pre-bookable burst slots per week). Final confirmation pending the PO + signed capacity-exception ticket (we will attach the runbook).

Next steps for Acme:
1) Please share a PO referencing deal ACME-1257 and billing to Acme AI, Inc.
2) Standard net30 is fine; if you need tax forms or SOW language let us know and we can route to Legal.
3) Procurement: confirm an authorized signer and send PO to billing@redwood.ai.

I'll also attach a short MOU to align expectations (attachment: acme_po_draft.pdf).

Cheers —
Marcus Lin
Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Kelly <ben.kelly@acme.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Procurement - Acme AI <procurement@acme.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 24 Nov 2026 11:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: STAGING: eval-lane reserve request & procurement handshake

Marcus / team —

Appreciate the fast turnaround. Procurement will issue a PO today referencing ACME-1257 with net30. Signed by our Finance head. We accept the scheduled burst model (will book windows 72 hours ahead).

One ask: can Redwood provide a short runbook snippet describing the eviction fallback (how we will be informed, and expected interruption behavior)? We'll include it in the run plan.

Ben Kelly
Director, AI Ops
Acme AI

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Kelly <ben.kelly@acme.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 24 Nov 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: STAGING: eval-lane reserve request & procurement handshake

Ben / Marcus / team —

Confirmed: Ops will schedule the transient carveout to begin Mon, Nov 30 at 08:00 PT and run through Jan 11 inclusive (6 weeks). We will provision 4 GPUs reserved Mon–Fri 08:00–20:00 PT. Two scheduled burst slots per week may be requested and must be pre-booked via the shared calendar (72-hour lead).

Eviction/runbook summary (for your run plan):
- If pool contention requires preemption, Acme will receive a 30-minute eviction notice via email + PagerDuty (if enabled).
- On eviction, Redwood will automatically redirect requests to an approved fallback model tier (lower memory footprint). Long-running KV priming will not be preserved; estimate 3–7 minutes to rewarm depending on sequence lengths.
- We will provide a runbook snippet in Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-eval-runbooks (doc: eval_eviction_runbook.md).

Attachments: acme_po_draft.pdf, staging_eval_headroom.csv

Thanks —
Laura Bennett
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Allocation Services
Redwood Inference
